test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 24 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Rati travels from City A to City B. If Rati drives her car at 1/3 of her normal speed, then she reaches City B 50 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Rati would take to travel from City A to City B if she drove at her normal speed.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **distance** is constant, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time**.

Speed ratio = 3 : 1 → Time ratio = 1 : 3.

Difference in time ratio = 3 − 1 = 2 units → 50 minutes.

1 unit = 25 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5cb6c2bd4c8679dbbe5acccf1ccea7c697c5895c19f51894e0725ec051138c03.png] 

**Given:** Reduced speed = 1/3 of normal speed, Time delay = 50 minutes.

**Formula Used:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed (Time ∝ 1/Speed when distance is constant).

⇒ Let normal speed be S and normal time be T.

⇒ New speed = S/3, so New time = 3T.

⇒ 3T − T = 50 minutes.

⇒ 2T = 50 minutes.

⇒ T = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion Rule

If speed becomes a/b of original speed, the new time becomes b/a of original time, provided distance remains the same.

Average Speed

For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

In the same direction, speed is subtracted (u − v). In opposite directions, speed is added (u + v).</p
